data.title: Duba Port Customs Thwarts Smuggling of 2.3 Million Amphetamine Pills Hidden in Concrete Bricks
data.content:
Riyadh, November 20, 2026, SPA -- Duba Port customs has thwarted six attempts to smuggle 2,305,695 amphetamine pills concealed within shipments arriving in the Kingdom through the port.
Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) spokesperson Hamoud Al-Harbi stated that six trucks arriving via Duba Port underwent standard customs inspections, revealing the narcotic pills hidden inside the hollow cavities of concrete bricks transported on the trucks. Following the seizure, coordination with the General Directorate of Narcotics Control led to the arrest of the intended recipient inside the Kingdom.
Al-Harbi affirmed ZATCA's commitment to maintaining strict customs oversight across all ports of entry to safeguard society against smuggling attempts in close cooperation with the Ministry of Interior and the General Directorate of Narcotics Control. He urged the public to report smuggling offenses and violations of the Unified Customs Law confidentially via the security hotline 1910, email 1910@zatca.gov.sa, or the international number 009661910, noting that financial rewards are granted for verified reports.
-- SPA
